## Cache protocol

### REQ-PROTO-001 — HTTP cache round trip

The server shall store a blob on PUT, return the identical bytes on GET, report existence and size on HEAD, and return 404 for a key that has no entry.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md "Why this exists"; docs/gradle.md; docs/docker-deploy.md "Verify it is working"; internal/server/server.go*

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-PROTO-001-AC1 | Given a running server with an empty store; when a client PUTs a body to /some-key and then GETs /some-key; then the PUT returns 201, the GET returns 200 with byte-identical content and a correct Content-Length | http-integration | yes | approved | 1 item(s) |
| REQ-PROTO-001-AC2 | Given a stored key; when a client sends HEAD for that key and GET for an absent key; then HEAD returns 200 with the stored size and no body; the GET of the absent key returns 404 | http-integration | yes | approved | 2 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-002 — Request path is the cache key

The server shall treat the entire request path, with the leading slash removed, as the cache key - no path prefix exists and none is required on either side. This requirement covers only the non-reserved cache namespace: the reserved application paths ("/", /healthz, /metrics, /statusz) are outside it, their GET behavior is specified by their own requirements (REQ-OBS-001, REQ-OBS-002, REQ-OBS-003, REQ-PROTO-006), and reserved-path write handling is specified by REQ-PROTO-007.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: docs/gradle.md "trailing slash"; docs/docker-deploy.md; internal/server/server.go cacheEndpoint*

> Recorded at review (Sep 10): a PUT to a reserved path such as /healthz is currently accepted into the cache namespace while its GET answers with the endpoint response. DECIDED (owner, 2026-09-11): reserved paths refuse writes — REQ-PROTO-007 is the contract, and the server change ships in v0.2.0.

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-PROTO-002-AC1 | Given a running server; when a client PUTs to an ordinary, non-reserved cache path such as /a/nested/key and GETs the same path; then the round trip succeeds, the same bytes are not visible under any other path, and the reserved endpoints continue to answer as endpoints | http-integration | yes | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-003 — Key validation

The server shall reject, with HTTP 400, any key whose segments are not 1-255 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._-], any key of more than 16 segments, any empty key, and any "." or ".." segment; path traversal shall not be able to escape the store root.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: docs/docker-deploy.md "Verify it is working"; internal/blobstore/blobstore.go ValidateKey*

> Recorded at review (Sep 10): Go's HTTP router redirects some dot-segment and repeated-slash paths (e.g. /a/../b, /a//b, /a/./b answer 307 to the normalized path) BEFORE key validation runs, so a helper-level test cannot stand in for this HTTP contract, and a redirect-following client may resubmit to the normalized key. DECIDED (owner, 2026-09-11): malformed keys are REJECTED with HTTP 400 through the real router — never normalized, no redirects. IMPLEMENTED (v0.2.0): a front controller ahead of ServeMux (internal/server.go newFrontController/rawPathIsMalformed) rejects a raw path with an empty, ".", or ".." segment (literal or percent-encoded) with 400 before ServeMux can redirect; verified by TestMalformedPathsRejectedNoRedirect with redirect-following disabled. A weaker check must not certify the stronger promise.

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-PROTO-003-AC1 | Given a running server, exercised through its real HTTP routing stack by a client that does NOT follow redirects; when the client requests keys containing a space, a "..", an empty segment, a 17th segment, or a 256-character segment - each in raw and percent-encoded form; then every such request receives HTTP 400 - a 307 redirect is a failure of this criterion, not proof - and no request mutates the store or creates a file outside the store root | http-integration | yes | approved | 3 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-005 — Body-size cap

The server shall reject a PUT whose body exceeds FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES with HTTP 413, without storing a partial entry; the default cap shall be 1 GiB.

### REQ-PROTO-006 — Browser landing page

The server shall answer a browser GET of the bare root with an HTML landing page (HTTP 200) rather than an error, without shadowing any cache key.

### REQ-PROTO-007 — Reserved paths refuse writes

PUT and DELETE to the reserved application paths ("/", /healthz, /metrics, /statusz) shall return HTTP 405 with "Allow: GET, HEAD" and shall store nothing: the reserved namespace is read-only, and a write aimed at it is a client error, never a silent cache entry.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: owner decision 2026-09-11; resolving the reserved-path backlog entry from the Sep 10 PR 43 review*

## Configuration

### REQ-CFG-001 — Configuration surface and defaults

The server shall be configured solely by environment variables: FSCACHE_ADDR (default ":8080"), FSCACHE_DATA_DIR (default "./data"), FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES (default 0, unbounded), FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES (default 1 GiB), FSCACHE_USERNAME and FSCACHE_PASSWORD (default unset). No runtime reconfiguration surface shall exist.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md configuration table; docs/docker-deploy.md "Configuration"; cmd/fscache/main.go*

### REQ-CFG-002 — Credentials are both-or-neither

The server shall refuse to start when exactly one of FSCACHE_USERNAME and FSCACHE_PASSWORD is set, with an error naming both variables.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md configuration table "required together"; cmd/fscache/main.go run*

### REQ-CFG-003 — Invalid configuration fails startup

The server shall refuse to start when a numeric configuration variable (FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES, FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES) is unparseable, carries trailing garbage, is negative, or overflows, exiting non-zero with a message naming the variable and the offending value. It shall never silently substitute a default for an invalid value: a typo in a size cap must stop the server, not unbound the cache.

## Authentication

### REQ-AUTH-001 — Basic Auth on the cache surface

When credentials are configured, the server shall require HTTP Basic Auth on every cache request and on the status surfaces, answering unauthenticated or wrong-credential requests with 401 and a WWW-Authenticate header, and never storing or serving data for them.

### REQ-AUTH-005 — Read-only credentials

In addition to the read-write credential pair, the server shall support an optional read-only credential pair (FSCACHE_RO_USERNAME and FSCACHE_RO_PASSWORD, default unset). Read-only credentials authenticate exactly like read-write credentials for GET and HEAD on every authenticated surface, and receive HTTP 403 with nothing stored for PUT and DELETE: developer laptops read, only the identities holding the read-write pair write. Configuration is fail-closed: the pair is both-or-neither, requires the read-write pair to be configured, and its username must differ from the read-write username.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: github issue 8 "read-only client mode"; competitive-2026-09*

## HTTP

### REQ-HTTP-001 — Server timeouts

The HTTP server shall run with explicit timeouts, generous where a legitimate cache transfer is slow and tight where only a stuck or idle connection waits - ReadHeaderTimeout 10s, IdleTimeout 120s, and read/write deadlines of 20 minutes per request (enough for the documented 1 GiB body cap over a slow CI link, roughly 0.9 MB/s sustained, and finite where today is infinite). The values are configuration constants proposed by engineering on 2026-09-11 and adjustable by requirement change, not by silent edit.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: test-strategy.md section 2.3; audit section 19*

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-HTTP-001-AC1 | Given the constructed HTTP server; when its timeout configuration is examined; then ReadHeaderTimeout is 10s, IdleTimeout is 120s, and ReadTimeout and WriteTimeout are 20 minutes - none unset | unit | yes | approved | 2 item(s) |

### REQ-HTTP-002 — Bounded concurrent uploads

The server shall bound concurrent PUT processing: at most FSCACHE_MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS uploads in flight (default 32; 0 disables the bound), with excess requests refused with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header, storing nothing. Build clients treat any error as a cache miss, so a refused upload degrades a build's caching, never the build. Slow clients can therefore hold at most a bounded number of upload slots, temp files, and file handles.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: test-strategy.md section 2.3; audit section 19*

## Storage

### REQ-STORE-001 — Durable storage across restart

Stored entries shall survive a clean server restart: a key stored before shutdown shall be retrievable, byte-identical, after the process is stopped and started against the same data directory.

### REQ-STORE-004 — A stored reply means a stored entry

A PUT shall succeed only when the blob is on disk AND its metadata record is written: if the metadata record fails, the server shall remove the blob and fail the PUT. A cache that says "stored" has stored it — retrievable, indexed, counted, and evictable.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: audit-response-2026-09-08 §4.7 (decided); test-strategy.md §2.2; audit §18*

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |

### REQ-STORE-005 — Startup reconciliation after unclean shutdown

The server shall write a marker file at startup and remove it on clean shutdown. When the marker is present at startup (an unclean exit), the server shall reconcile the two stores before serving: blobs without a metadata record are adopted (size from disk, recency now), records without a blob are dropped, stale temporary files are removed, totals are recomputed, and the reconciliation counts are logged. Blobs are truth; metadata is a rebuildable index. Clean restarts skip the walk.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: audit-response-2026-09-08 §4.7 (decided); test-strategy.md §2.2; audit §18*

| REQ-STORE-005-AC2 | Given a metadata record whose blob is missing; when reconciliation runs; then the record is dropped and totals no longer include it | component | yes | approved | 2 item(s) |

## Eviction

### REQ-EVICT-001 — Size-capped LRU eviction

With FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES set, the server shall bound the COMMITTED LIVE-CACHE BLOB BYTES - the total size of indexed, retrievable entries, measured after an operation completes - by evicting least-recently-used entries; with the cap at 0 the store shall be unbounded. This is a bounded live-cache size with documented temporary headroom, not a hard filesystem quota: temporary and in-flight disk usage during writes, and concurrent-write headroom, are outside this requirement and need requirements of their own before any hard disk ceiling is claimed.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md "Full core"; docs/docker-deploy.md "Sizing"; internal/cache/cache.go*

> Recorded at review (Sep 10): the implementation writes the incoming object before evicting, and an entry LARGER than the whole cap is accepted and then immediately evicted itself (write succeeds, read returns not-found, indexed total returns to zero). The oversized- entry policy is an open product decision in backlog.yaml; this criterion is therefore limited to entries that individually fit within the cap, so it describes the extracted contract without silently strengthening it. DECIDED (owner, 2026-09-11): oversized entries are rejected — REQ-EVICT-002 is the contract, and the server change ships in v0.2.0.

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-EVICT-001-AC1 | Given a server with a small cap, holding entries that exceed it in aggregate, where each entry's individual size is at most the cap; when a new entry no larger than the cap is stored; then least-recently-used entries are removed until the new entry fits, the new entry is retrievable afterward, and the committed live-cache blob bytes, measured after the operation completes, do not exceed the cap | component | yes | approved | 3 item(s) |
| REQ-EVICT-001-AC2 | Given a capped store where an old key is re-read; when eviction next runs; then the re-read key is treated as recently used and outlives never-read older entries | component |  | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-EVICT-002 — Oversized entries are rejected, not churned

A PUT whose entry is larger than the configured cache cap (FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES, when set) shall be rejected with HTTP 413 and the response header "X-FSCache-Reject: entry-exceeds-cache-cap", storing nothing and evicting nothing. This rejection is distinct from the body-limit rejection (REQ-PROTO-005): a request over FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES is refused for its size on the wire and does not carry this header; a request over the cache cap is refused because it can never live in the cache, and says so. Build clients treat any 413 as a cache miss, so a build containing such an artifact completes normally without remote caching for it.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: owner decision 2026-09-11; resolving the oversized-entry backlog entry from the Sep 10 PR 43 review*

## Observability

### REQ-OBS-001 — Liveness endpoint

The server shall answer GET /healthz with HTTP 200 and body "ok" for as long as the process is serving. /healthz is a liveness check only: it does not look at the data directory, the disk, or the store, so it never reports a full, read-only, or otherwise failing data directory. Operators who need to alert on disk trouble use the fscache_store_writable, fscache_store_free_bytes, and fscache_put_errors_total metrics (REQ-OBS-002).

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md quickstart; docs/docker-deploy.md; internal/server/server.go handleHealthz; owner decision 2026-10-09 (backlog 13 (a)+(c)); advisor step 5 2026-10-09*

### REQ-OBS-002 — Prometheus metrics

GET /metrics shall expose, in Prometheus format, at least fscache_http_requests_total (by method and status), fscache_cache_hits_total, fscache_cache_misses_total, fscache_bytes_read_total, fscache_bytes_written_total, fscache_http_request_duration_seconds, fscache_evicted_entries_total, fscache_store_bytes, and fscache_store_entries, and fscache_store_writable, fscache_store_free_bytes, and fscache_put_errors_total (by reason). The last three describe disk trouble; /healthz never does (REQ-OBS-001). The counters shall move with real traffic.

## Privacy

### REQ-PRIV-001 — No outbound connections

The server shall make no outbound network connections — no telemetry, no update check, no licence check, no name resolution — at rest or under load, and shall run identically on a host with no route to the internet.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: SECURITY.md "Data handling"; README.md security section; www "What we do not collect"*

## FIPS 140-3

### REQ-FIPS-001 — Validated-module FIPS build

The -fips build shall link Go's CMVP-validated FIPS 140-3 cryptographic module (certificate #5247), selected at build time by GOFIPS140. Enabled mode alone is not this requirement: a standard build can enable FIPS mode at runtime (GODEBUG=fips140=on) without containing the frozen validated module, so evidence must establish the module identity, not just the mode.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md "Image variants"; docs/install.md FIPS section; .goreleaser.yaml fscache-fips*

| REQ-FIPS-001-AC2 | Given a binary built WITHOUT the validated module selected, running with FIPS mode enabled at runtime (GODEBUG=fips140=on); when the same evidence check runs against it; then it does NOT pass — the check distinguishes the validated-module build from a merely mode-enabled build | acceptance-release-artifact | yes | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-FIPS-002 — FIPS posture observable and truthful at runtime

The startup log and /statusz shall report the actual FIPS operating mode and the actual module identity truthfully in every runtime configuration, including runtime overrides: a -fips build in its default runtime configuration reports active with its module identified; a standard build in its default configuration reports off; and a standard build with FIPS mode enabled at runtime (GODEBUG=fips140=on) shall not claim the validated module or its certificate. The report shall never state more than the binary can know about itself.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: docs/install.md; docs/offline-install.md; internal/buildinfo*

> Known discrepancy at extraction, recorded in backlog.yaml: the current internal/buildinfo note hardcodes the certificate label behind a mode check, so a runtime-enabled standard build would overstate its posture. The product fix is later requirements-first work, not part of this baseline PR.

### REQ-REL-004 — Continuous scan gate and toolchain freshness

A newly disclosed vulnerability shall be caught before release, not on tag day: the full scanner set shall run as a required check on every pull request, every push to main, and every tag; scanner installers shall be pinned by checksum so a scanner that cannot run fails the pipeline rather than passing silently; main's latest candidate shall be rescanned daily; and the Go toolchain shall be kept on its latest patch by an automated bump.

## DEP

### REQ-DEP-001 — Dependabot majors are judged by a machine

A Dependabot major version bump shall be judged by the Dependabot reviewer, not by a person: from main, hourly, it gathers the evidence with no model involved, has two readers rank findings without a verdict, and decides mechanically to merge or to hold with an issue; it posts its result as a check and edits nothing.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/dependabot-reviewer.yml; bin/dependabot-reviewer.py*

## SUP

### REQ-SUP-001 — Actions supply-chain checks

Our workflows shall take no new version of an action, or of a tool, image or package they download, until it has been public 7 days; shall check every version we use, every day, against the public advisory and malware lists; and shall say publicly only what they know.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml; .github/dependabot.yml; .github/supply-chain-exceptions.json*

> AC14 design decision (Codex round 1, B2): a non-plain version of a table tool is a HIT only on the records the databases return for it. A version with no OSV record and no GitHub advisory (cosign@latest, or the (default) pins of cosign and kind in the real tree) reads clean, deliberately: with no record nothing is known to be affected at any version, and making every non-plain pin a hit would open a daily issue forever with nothing to report. The rule is about the verdict on records, not about the pin. AC14 evaluation: range events are evaluated as OSV evaluates them: sorted by version (introduced 0 is the minimum, at one version the fixed wins), last_affected inclusive; Go versions compare as strict semver (pseudo-versions, numeric pre-releases and +incompatible are valid; r1, p1, post1 and rev1 are pre-release identifiers). A limit event is refused in SEMVER and ECOSYSTEM ranges (the record is a hit, a fail-closed refusal): the Go vulnerability database never writes limit, the OSV schema text could not be consulted offline, so any use of it in a Go range is treated as unreadable, which also removes the any-or-all question for several limits (the evaluator, used for other ecosystems, reads below ANY limit as affected). The schema asks for id and modified on a record, ecosystem and name on a package, an introduced event in every range (their order is free), and not both fixed and last_affected in one range; aliases may be absent or null. An independent interval oracle in the test compares the evaluator on a generated grid. The 240 recorded verdicts did not change. AC14 residual: the rule judges the OSV record's affected entries only; GitHub's ranges are read as before. An OSV answer that is not a record (not an object, no string id or modified) is a hit under the id UNREADABLE-OSV-RECORD; a GIT range together with a SEMVER or ECOSYSTEM range in one entry is a hit in every branch. The gh and git calls of pin-audit.py and of the shared helpers in pin-age-check.py have a 120 s timeout that stops the run (exit 2). AC14 residual (semver): bounds that SemVer 2.0.0 forbids (a numeric pre-release identifier with a leading zero such as 3.0.0-01, an empty identifier in the pre-release or the build metadata) are unparsable and read as affected, so the record is a hit. Go pseudo-versions with a zero-time stamp (0.0.0-00010101000000-000000000000) are one valid alphanumeric identifier, because it contains a hyphen, and parse normally. AC15 limit: the pins nested inside an action are not counted as held, so a ruling for a pin that is only nested can be dormant, never dead. AC15 expectation (step 8, Oct 9): the three cosign rulings (GO-2024-2718, GO-2024-2719, GO-2023-2181) are ALIVE now because main pinned cosign 3.1.3 inside the 90-day history window (until commit 8a7512d); they become dormant (or dead, if a cosign 3.1.3 pin has appeared and they decide nothing) about 2026-12-14, 90 days after that pin left main, unless a cosign 3.1.3 pin is held again (pull request 249). Finding at step 6 (Oct 9): with the corrected table paths, the existing package-name filter of the audit already clears cosign 3.1.3 against GO-2026-4309. The real work of AC14 is (1) the corrected table (goreleaser, osv and golangci-lint need their /v2 path), (2) GitHub names matched under both the bare and the /vMAJOR path so the five existing rulings keep working, (3) the log of ignored entries, (4) the OSV query by the /vMAJOR path.

## REPO

### REQ-REPO-001 — Branch hygiene without a human

The repository shall remove its own stale branches with no human step and never remove a good one: a daily sweep deletes a remote branch whose pull request is merged or closed, or that has no pull request and no commit for 14 days, and never touches the default branch, release branches, Dependabot branches, a branch with an open pull request, a branch that is the base of an open pull request, or a branch kept by an unexpired entry in a keep-file on the default branch; every deletion is logged with its commit so it can be restored; and a local script prunes the lane's own stale local branches and worktrees without losing work.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/reserved-branch-guard.yml; bin/branch-sweep.py; bin/local-prune.sh; .github/branch-keep.json*

> The sweep is a scheduled job inside the existing reserved-branch-guard workflow (no new workflow file). Its planner is bin/branch-sweep.py; the keep-file is .github/branch-keep.json, an object {"keep": [{"branch", "expires" (YYYY-MM-DD), "reason"}]} read through the API at the default branch. The sweeper reads the runner's response headers by lower-case key (link). Local prune finds gone branches in a dry run with git ls-remote --heads origin (read-only); only --apply may run git fetch --prune. Branches on forks are out of scope.

## CHAIN

### REQ-CHAIN-001 — The Sign job is its own workflow file and cannot be reached from Build

The release provenance shall be written and signed keyless by a Sign job that lives in its own workflow file, runs on its own fresh GitHub-hosted runner, never runs code from the build, receives only Build's digests, and whose signing identity no other job can obtain, so that a malicious Build step cannot produce provenance that Release accepts (SLSA Build Level 3 design).

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-sign.yml; .github/workflows/release.yml; bin/chain-verify.py; bin/chain-hostile-step.sh; .github/policy/chain-signers.json; .github/policy/chain-scripts.json*

> stage-sign.yml is the one new workflow file v0.3.0 adds (rule 52). PR 1 builds the Sign side and the verify side; Release's own signing of the policy (rule 57) is PR 4. Public copy says "designed to SLSA Build Level 3", never "certified" (rule 50a, 84). REQ-REL-008-AC1 changed from 25 to 26 files because rule 52 ratifies exactly one new workflow file, stage-sign.yml (owner RATIFIED Oct 9 2026 11:51 EDT, ops/docs/ratify/2026-10-09-v030-rules.md). Step-8 round 1 (Opus and Sonnet, advisor 0343 process): the hand-code attempt of the dry run uses `chain-verify.py check-build-record` (the same refusals as `sign --check`, no signer, no cosign), so no job other than stage-sign.yml names the signing subcommand and the earlier exemption for jobs without id-token is gone; a workflow_dispatch on a TAG is refused by `sign --check` and the hostile input is limited to a branch ref (`inputs.dry-run == true && github.ref_type == 'branch'`); the build call of a dry run runs in snapshot mode (admission is skipped on a manual run, which used to skip build, sign and both hostile jobs), publishes no GitHub attestation and needs no admission artifact. RUNTIME PROOF OF AC5 (advisor accepted Oct 10 (lane AC)): the GitHub dry run cannot be green in this pull request, because Build writes no `witness-build` record or `digests.json` until PR 2 and the sixth case needs a throwaway second-caller workflow on the dry-run ref; PR 1 merges only to chain-v030, and the proof runs and is linked when PR 2 (Build) lands there. CUTOVER CHECKLIST: the cutover pull request (chain-v030 to main) does not merge without a green rc-tag run of the same commit's chain files, linked (the REQ-CHAIN-001-AC5 GitHub proof; advisor 0383), and one genuine cosign v3.1.3 bundle from it has passed `chain-verify.py verify` (the Rekor inclusionPromise question of REQ-CHAIN-002). Dry run (pipeline design, round 5-6; advisor to confirm): on a workflow_dispatch on a branch Sign writes a record marked dryRun and its SAN ref is the branch; such a record can only be judged under a dry_run policy by the dry run's own verify job (stage sign only), while Release makes its policy with --tag, every stage-start refuses a dry_run policy, and a provenance carrying dryRun true is refused under any non-dry policy; the jobs after Sign carry no tag-ref conjunct of their own (release.yml's image to promotion jobs have only `!inputs.dry-run`): the tag guard reaches them through needs, because build requires admission.result == 'success' outside a dry run and admission runs only on a v* tag (bin/chain-sign-wiring-test.sh, case R8).

### REQ-CHAIN-002 — Timestamps, the transparency log and the per-tag release policy

Every keyless signature in the release chain shall carry Sigstore's public timestamp so it can be checked after its ten-minute certificate expires, everything a customer verifies shall have an entry in Rekor, and each tag shall have a release policy made from a committed template that accepts exactly the stage identities of that tag and no others.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/policy/release-policy.template.json; bin/chain-verify.py; .github/policy/sigstore-trust.json*

> Status: - Round 7: `policy make` and `sign --check` take the committed trust file and the three PEMs next to the template as defaults (overridable by flags), with the same trust-hash check, so the first signed rc-tag run's and Release's pinned lines pass no file flags. PR 1 writes the template and the verify side only; Release signing the finished policy (rule 57) is PR 4. Witness's stage records cannot go to Rekor (Witness has no Rekor support); they carry the timestamp authority's stamp and are kept as release evidence (rule 53b). Decisions: - Step-8 round 1: - (a) the certificate chain is checked against the policy's root ONLY (the system trust store is switched off with -no-CAfile -no-CApath -no-CAstore -trusted), and tested with an attacker CA in SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR; - (b) timestamps come in two forms, a bare token in Witness records (go-witness timestamp/tsp.go) and a whole DER TimeStampResponse in a Sigstore bundle (protobuf-specs sigstore_common.proto), read by their type; - (c) Rekor is pinned to v1 by .github/policy/cosign-signing-config.json (cosign v3.1.3 `--signing-config`, an advisor-visible change to the pinned cosign command line: the default would use the TUF signing config, which may name Rekor v2 with no signed entry timestamp), and the log key in the trust file is the v1 key only; - (e) a record with a repeated JSON key or any signature count but one is refused. - Step-8 round 2 (NB-1, Opus): the certificate field of a record, and the verifier of a Rekor entry's body, must be EXACTLY ONE certificate PEM block with nothing but whitespace around it and no bytes after the certificate's outer SEQUENCE; the identity is read from that one DER and openssl verifies a PEM re-made from the same DER (before this, text or base64 before a genuine block was skipped by openssl but read as the identity by the homemade DER reader, so a self-made certificate with the right identity placed before any genuine certificate was accepted); every JSON reader is UTF-8 only (UTF-16/32 are refused, not guessed). - `sign --check` and `check-build-record` take exactly one of --template (the committed template: the per-tag policy is made there from GITHUB_REF) and --policy (a finished policy); the stage-sign.yml line and its pin changed from `--policy <template>` to `--template <template>`. - The flag `--rekor-stub` keeps its name only because later pull requests (PR 2-4) pin lines against it; it names the file of Rekor entries a bundle carries. - Opus N-9 is left as a documented note (no change). - Step-8 round 3 (B-1, both seats): the time of a timestamp is read ONLY from the bare token that the timestamp authority signed (a whole response is first required to have a clean status, no status string other than the TSA default ("unspecified") and no failure info, and is then reduced to its token with `openssl ts -reply -token_out`; the TSA's signature is verified over that same token), because a response's status section lies outside the TSA's signature and an edited statusString `x\nTime stamp: <date>` used to set the time compared with the certificate's validity; the stamp form is bound to the record type (a Witness collection carries the bare token `tsp`, the provenance the whole response `rfc3161-response`; the signed release policy either, PR 4 decides) and a mismatch is refused; a genTime with milliseconds is read and the fraction dropped; a certificate with a repeated extension (a second SAN, a second Build Config URI) is refused; the DER reader is not a general parser and trusts only the structure of a Fulcio-signed certificate. - `actions` follows a listed local composite action wherever it is stored, including under .github/workflows/, and skips following only a reference that names a .yml/.yaml file (a reusable workflow, judged as a workflow of its own). - The token of the key and token attempts must name exactly <repo>/.github/workflows/stage-sign.yml@<ref> of this repository (GITHUB_REPOSITORY). - Codex security round 1 (Oct 10): - (S1) after cosign, `sign` refuses a bundle with no or an empty timestamp list or Rekor entry list, naming each, verifies the two files it wrote as stage sign and requires the payload cosign signed to be, as parsed JSON with exact types (true is not 1, 1 is not 1.0), the statement Sign built (Opus round-1 verify F1, H2) before it prints ok; --out must not exist yet (., a folder, a file or a symlink is a usage error before anything runs) and any refusal, or any failure of that self-check, removes only the files Sign wrote and the folder it made (H1); - (S2) a Rekor entries file whose `entries` is not a list of objects is a refusal, never a traceback; - (S3) base64 must be canonical (re-encoding gives the same text) and JSON readers refuse NaN, Infinity, -Infinity and numbers that overflow to infinity (1e400); - (S4) only `actions` imports PyYAML; the Sign path runs on the standard library. - Codex security round 3 (Oct 10): an envelope field of the wrong JSON type is a refusal, and the issuer (.1.8) and Build Config URI (.1.18) extensions must each be one DER UTF8String TLV (Fulcio's v2 OID specification). - Codex security round 2 (Oct 10): every certificate of the Fulcio chain and of the TSA chain is checked AT the stamp's authenticated genTime (openssl -attime at the whole second below it, never -no_check_time), so an intermediate or a TSA signer that had expired, or was not yet valid, then is refused; genTime keeps its fraction (12:00:00.5 is after a certificate ending 12:00:00; for the certificate window openssl's check at the whole second below already decides, the fraction decides the 10-minute allowance after the verification clock, and a case pins that); a Rekor entry's logIndex and integratedTime must be canonical decimal strings, which fits the protobuf-JSON Sigstore bundle (int64 as strings): the Rekor REST API writes these fields as JSON numbers, which are refused, so the later pull request that produces the --rekor-stub file must take the entries from the bundle or emit protobuf-JSON strings; `sign` with no cosign on PATH is a refusal that removes the output folder it made. - Advisor reading, Oct 9 (handoff 0334; the ratified text is unchanged): a stage's identity in rules 52/52a/57 is the certificate whose SAN (Build Signer URI) is the stage file at the tag AND whose Build Config URI extension (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.18, the top-level workflow) is release.yml at the same tag, issued by GitHub's OIDC issuer; the policy pins all three. - Witness's own verify can check the issuer but not the Build Config URI (in-toto-witness options/verify.go:80-99), so bin/chain-verify.py checks it. Stated exclusions: - (d) the Rekor entry in the tests is SYNTHETIC but has the real fields (sigstore-go pkg/tlog/entry.go, protobuf-specs sigstore_rekor.proto, Rekor dsse 0.0.1); the first signed rc-tag run captures a genuine bundle to replace it, and confirms the cosign bundle shape and whether the issuer extension is .1.8 or .1.1; Open items: - OPEN until one genuine cosign v3.1.3 bundle is captured at the first signed rc-tag run (cutover checklist): the verifier requires a Rekor v1 inclusionPromise (signed entry timestamp); a proof-only entry (inclusion proof without a promise) would be refused. - The OIDC issuer is read from OID .1.8; the spike certificate dumps list .1.1 and not .1.8, so the first signed rc-tag run must confirm .1.8 is present on a real certificate.

### REQ-CHAIN-003 — Each stage verifies the one before it; only standard record types; every action pinned

Every stage after Build shall first verify the previous stage's signed record with one shared plain script and stop on failure, naming the stage; only Witness's standard records, SLSA provenance and the signed release policy shall exist as signed record types; every signed record shall have a distinct claim and a named consumer; and every action reference shall be a full commit digest and be on the committed allowed-actions list.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/chain-verify.py; .github/policy/allowed-actions.json; .github/policy/chain-records.json; .github/policy/chain-scripts.json; check-action-pins.py*

> Status: - The 14 REQ-CHAIN-001..003 ACs are `approved` here because the validator requires a requirement introduced under an approved baseline to carry its status; the English was validated by the advisor at step 5 (handoff 0328; readings 0334, 0343) and the rules ratified by the owner on Oct 9 2026 (rules 50-67). Controls: - The controls are review, the trusted pin-wiring judge (it requires the four chain suites as exact CI steps), the closed id-token list, and Release's SAN pin (REQ-CHAIN-001-AC4: only a Fulcio certificate whose SAN is stage-sign.yml at the tag is accepted). The hash lists are tripwires: a listed file changes only with a visible hash edit in the same pull request; a script edited together with its row in chain-scripts.json is caught only by review and the pinned judge, because the judge reads that JSON from the pull request's own tree. They are in the pull request's own control; an independent control would need CODEOWNERS or ruleset entries on .github/policy/** and bin/chain-*-test.sh, an owner permission change not made here. - Closed lists (.github/policy/): id-token-jobs.json, the jobs that may hold id-token: write, a reason each (any other holder, matched case-insensitively, a stale entry, or an unparsable workflow fails; a merge key, `<<` or `!!merge`, at any depth of any workflow or composite action is refused, and one that does not parse as a single YAML document is a finding; composite actions are found anywhere in the repository, any case); legacy-stage-files.json, the eleven legacy stage files PRs 2-4 rewrite, pinned by sha256 (the wiring and records judges leave out their own findings but follow the LISTED scripts they run and what they produce; an UNLISTED file they run is never scanned; a changed one is judged in full; the list goes with the last of them); build-config-files.json, the build configuration outside bin/ and .github/ pinned by sha256, with .goreleaser.yaml held to a closed key set, its two hooks, and each build (no repeated id) with env, flags and ldflags exactly as today; chain-signers.json, every non-provenance signing call with a reason; chain-scripts.json, the scripts a stage may run by sha256 (only bin/chain-verify.py may sign provenance). - The id-token list is per job: it closes unlisted jobs, including remote reusable workflows, in-process libraries, files outside bin/ and .github/, and tools missing from the signer table. A signer step added to a listed job is seen when the shared signer table names it (@actions/attest is in it); otherwise review and the pin checker see it. - Python puts a script's directory first on sys.path, so a file in bin/ named after a standard-library module would replace that module inside the Sign job, whose SAN really is stage-sign.yml (the SAN pin cannot see it). Closed structurally: the Sign step runs `python3 -I -B` and every python3 line of a stage file runs with -I; chain-verify.py compiles its two helper modules from their bytes after checking each against its sha256 in chain-scripts.json (no bytecode cache is consulted; tests prove a bin/fractions.py and an unchecked-hash __pycache__ copy are not run, and changed helper bytes are refused). The judge refuses any file or directory under bin/ or .github/ named after a standard-library module, and any __pycache__ directory or .pyc/.pyo/.so/.pyd/.dll file there (names matched case-insensitively). The -I rule covers stage-file lines only; a third-party name (bin/yaml.py) on a job without -I is backed by the file allowlist for bin/ and Release's SAN pin. Release's own `policy make` in stage-promote.yml runs with -I too. - Information, not a gap in Release: an unlisted file run by a frozen id-token job (bin/vex-forms.py, bin/patch-decide.py and the like) is not scanned by these suites; keyed signing is outside the keyless model (the only signing-like secret, AUDITOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, mints App tokens); neither can pass Release's SAN pin. Obfuscated signers are out of scope (owner, Oct 3); `docker buildx --attest type=provenance` writes unsigned provenance. Decisions: - AC3: no known-red allowance; the real tree is an ordinary `expect ok` with the frozen files' own findings left out. - AC4 is narrow on purpose: `actions` rejects today's release.yml, stage-build.yml and stage-promote.yml until PRs 2-4 rewrite them; it refuses repeated keys (trimmed, case-folded) and malformed shapes by name. The pin checker's repeated-key rule is its own pull request (pin-check-repeated-keys). - AC5 (narrowed, advisor 0334): only release.yml calls stage-sign.yml and no stage file calls another; scan.yml and main-candidate-rescan.yml stay allowed callers because the policy pins the Build Config URI. - `stage-start` starts only from rebuild<-build, check<-build, sign<-build and release<-{build, sign, rebuild, check}, with Sign's digest-format and subject-type checks. - CI: the four suites are steps of ci.yml's allowlist job, judging a copy of the tracked files; a lint case refuses any pipe into a quiet grep under pipefail. Stated exclusions: - A command built at run time inside a listed script; a signer reached only through an argv array or a program another program spawns; an unlisted file run by a frozen id-token job (backed by Release's SAN pin). A signer in a script outside chain-scripts.json run by a NON-stage listed job (bash bin/x.sh with cosign sign-blob, `go run .../cmd/cosign`, `gh attestation sign`, `npx @sigstore/cli`, rekor-cli) is not seen; it signs with that job's own OIDC identity, so the SAN is that workflow and Release's SAN pin (REQ-CHAIN-001-AC4) refuses it. Open items: - Cosign is Sign's tool (rule 53b needs a Rekor entry, which Witness cannot write).

### REQ-CHAIN-004 — Build runs sealed, under Witness, after admission, and hands Sign only a digest list

The Build stage shall be one workflow file and one identity holding two jobs, an apk matrix job (one runner per native architecture) and one assemble job, each directly on a GitHub-hosted VM and never in a container, in which Witness is installed first (pinned by checksum) and everything else runs as one committed script under Witness; that script first admits the tagged commit with every check the old admission stage made, then builds the package and the images with the cache lane's two scripts inside a network-less namespace, checks the built server reports its real version, and writes digests.json, the only thing Sign accepts; Witness's record is signed keyless under Build's own identity with the Sigstore timestamp and never contains the job's identity-token variables; Build holds no secret and no registry credential.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-build.yml; bin/build-stage.sh; bin/build-admit.py; bin/build-version-check.py*

A snapshot record is marked by its Witness step name (snapshot-apk, snapshot- build, snapshot-rapk, snapshot-rebuild), not by a field, and every reader applies ONE RULE to the collection name in one place (read_record and read_collection): a name that is exactly snapshot- followed by [a-z0-9_-]* is refused as a snapshot record, and any other name that is not exactly a release name of the stage that reads it (apk or build for Build, rapk or rebuild for Rebuild) is refused by `collection name ...`, so spelling variants and Unicode lookalikes are refused by name too. THIS RULE REFUSES HONEST CONFUSION EARLY, with a clear message; it is not the security boundary. The mode guard step compares case-sensitively in bash because GitHub's `==` in an expression is case-insensitive (inputs.mode == 'Snapshot' is true), so the guard is load-bearing: a looser guard would let a mixed-case mode skip both Witness steps. AC15 reads NAMES only: it looks at product-subject file names of a record and at the keys of a digests.json, never at the digest values (a value cannot carry a version). Snapshot-rapk is a real step (AC7): the AC13 clause that said bind had no snapshot-rapk step is struck, which is an English AC edit that needs the advisor's or owner's ratification line (the advisor already accepted snapshot-rapk in AC7). Hardening note only: the callers judge reads YAML with a loader that keeps the last of two equal keys; a duplicate-key-refusing loader would close that, and is not changed here. F2 (step-6 round 3): the real-Go proof is in bin/chain-snapshot-test.sh. With v0.3.0 at HEAD the single line git tag --force v0.0.0-rc.1 HEAD still leaves the Go stamp v0.3.0 (the test's control); the delete, make and check lines give the stamp v0.0.0-rc.1 with vcs.revision equal to HEAD, leave the remote untouched and are idempotent. The test skips cleanly, still counted, when go or git is missing; the CI runner has both. artifact-acceptance (AC14, step-6 round 3, F3): the value SHAPE of expected-checksums changes, from the raw checksums.txt text to the one-line digests JSON, and the artifact it reads is Build's dist (the four Linux archives) instead of dist-snapshot. The callee stage-acceptance-artifacts.yml's handling of the JSON form and of the artifact name dist is PR 3's change (Check absorbs it), so until PR 3 merges on chain-v030 that job is EXPECTED RED on the integration branch; this lane changes the call only, as cache-3f's option (b). The guard is tested with real git (unset, empty, false, FALSE, TRUE, 1 and 'true ' all refuse and leave every tag) and its position before the first git tag is asserted in the wiring test. ### REQ-CHAIN-005 — Rebuild repeats the build on a fresh machine and blocks on any difference

The Rebuild stage shall be one workflow file and one identity (the same two-job shape as Build: an apk matrix job and an assemble job) on fresh GitHub-hosted VMs that first verifies Build's signed record, then builds the same commit with the same pinned tools, the same two scripts and the same build date, compares every digest with Build's record, signs only a verdict under its own identity naming each differing item, and runs alongside Check, needing only Build.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-reproducibility.yml; bin/build-stage.sh; bin/chain-verify.py; .github/workflows/release.yml*

> Release publishes Build's bytes and never Rebuild's (rule 64), so Rebuild's only output is its verdict. The compared items follow cache's interface note: per-architecture apk (apk-tool.py digest), local index, modules SBOM, inputs manifest, full lock file, the OCI image index digest and each per-architecture manifest digest (OUT/<variant>.digest and .manifests), the SBOM files and the binary; the layout of the apkindex, inputs manifest and binary items is PROPOSED/UNVERIFIED in the tests. Snapshot Rebuild (AC7; advisor validation of the snapshot step 5, Oct 9): the PR gate's reproducibility check keeps its two independent assemblies in snapshot form; the snapshot Rebuild has no signature to verify (a snapshot record is refused by verify and stage-start), so its trust in Build's items.json is the hash the snapshot-build record holds for it, checked by rebuild-compare --snapshot inside the same workflow run.

### REQ-AUD-018 — The auditor review gate accepts a recorded substitute for the second reviewer

The auditor shall keep everything auditor-related in the auditor directory, hold its Python to the same 100% coverage gate as the Go, and let no change to the auditor merge without a review record cleared by the independent second review; the review gate may accept a recorded, time-boxed substitute for the second reviewer (AC4 onward), and nothing else: only for the codex seat, only by an opus entry named in a reviewed allow-list on the default branch, only before that entry's expiry, and never for the Sonnet review.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: auditor directory bin/auditor-review-gate.py; auditor directory bin/auditor-layout-check.py; auditor directory tests/coverage-gate.sh; auditor directory reviews/substitutes.json; .github/workflows/agent-review-gate.yml; .github/workflows/ci.yml*

> The `then` text of AC1, AC2 and AC3 is a PARAPHRASE of the ratified sentences with the literal auditor path replaced by 'the auditor directory' (the layout check forbids that literal in this file); the VERBATIM ratified sentences are quoted in the comments above the three entries in test-evidence/mappings.yaml, which is exempt from the layout check. Back-fill of AC1 to AC3 (status approved on the matrix page's ratification; the then text of each is the page's English apart from one substitution, the literal auditor path written as "the auditor directory", which the layout check forces in this file). Also recorded: the review gate exempts the review-record files themselves (reviews/<64 hex>.json) from AC3's "every change", because a record cannot review itself. Also recorded: the review gate's scope is wider than AC3's text: its guarded set also covers bin/check-file-allowlist.sh, bin/check-file-allowlist-test.sh and the gate workflow, which live outside the auditor directory (an English-vs-code difference like the AC1 exemptions; not edited here). The evidence for "before merge" (AC3) and for the "required coverage job" (AC2) shows the checks exist and run in CI; that the main branch ruleset REQUIRES them is not checkable from the repository and is recorded here as an inspection item for the owner's settings. AC1 exemptions in the layout check beyond the AC text: .github/dependabot.yml and .githooks/pre-commit (read as allowlist entries; not named in the ratified English, pending the advisor), plus the two amendments above (mappings.yaml and unmapped.yaml, owner Oct 2; bin/patch-decide.py and its test, owner Oct 3). The layout checker's docstring still lists only the workflow files and the allowlist entries (stale; follow-up). ### REQ-AUD-019 — The auditor unit tests touch no real system path

The auditor's Python unit tests shall not open, list, create, link, stat or resolve any real system path: a runtime guard armed for the whole test run fails any such call that leaves the test's temporary directory, the repository checkout and the interpreter's own environment; the Python tests are also scanned statically in full for a system-path literal outside a reviewed allow-list; and every other test script (shell) is scanned statically only for a symbolic link made to an absolute target and for creating files without a temporary directory. Go and Java tests are not scanned statically; the runtime guard covers whatever test discovery actually runs.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: auditor directory bin/tests/fs_guard.py; auditor directory bin/tests/test_fs_guard.py; auditor directory bin/tests/system_path_allowlist.py*

> The runtime guard is an audit hook plus wrappers installed by test_0000_arm_fs_guard.py, the first module discovery imports (digits sort before letters; test_fs_guard.py asserts that it sorts first and that an early and a late module are both guarded). Import-time code of a module that sorted before it would be unguarded; none does, and a new one named test_0* before it would fail that assertion; it judges the resolved path of each call (symbolic links followed, ".." applied after a link, a dir_fd or an open fd resolved to its directory) against the temporary directory, the checkout and the interpreter environment (read only), and is proven by mutants run in a container. The static literal scan keeps a reviewed allow-list (system_path_allowlist.py) whose whole-file rows pin the file byte for byte. The shell scan is limited to ln -s / cp -s (and the hard-link form) with an absolute target and to a script that creates files without ever calling mktemp or tempfile (the mktemp rule); the scan does not check that every file lands under the temp directory, the runtime guard (AC1) is what catches a stray path. The shell checks are a lint of plain forms, not a security control. The static scans read only git-tracked files and skip test_fs_guard.py itself and the coverage gate script; Python helpers outside the test file name pattern (fixtures, fs_guard.py) are not literal-scanned; a metadata exemption listed in AC1 (ancestors of a root, sysconfig directories, the stdlib zip, pyvenv.cfg, the trusted user base, /dev/null and /dev/urandom, descriptors open at arming, ctypes.CDLL(None)) is deliberate, not a gap. A container job whose HOME is not the account's home directory loses the user-scheme metadata entries (coverage stats them); the guard then refuses, it does not widen. The runtime guard is a tripwire for accidental access to real system paths by the repository's own tests; it is not a security boundary against test code that deliberately subverts it (replacing the SQLite authorizer, swallowing the refusal, or altering sys.path). Documented residuals of the runtime guard (it is a tripwire, see AC1): a test can replace the SQLite authorizer with set_authorizer; a refusal can be swallowed by an except Exception that catches the SQLite DatabaseError, or by asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True) in the main thread; a C library that opens a file without emitting an audit event (ssl, posix.stat) is not seen; other runners than discovery (python -m unittest <module>, the direct test_panel_sdk_probe.py run in ci.yml, pytest) do not arm the guard; and a package that sorts before the arming module would be imported unguarded. PLAIN FORMS ONLY (AC2): the Python literal scan detects an absolute path whose first component is one of a fixed name list (etc usr var private Library System opt bin sbin dev home root proc sys Users tmp Applications Volumes run srv lib lib64 boot mnt nix cores Network snap workspace github media data afs net scratch export exports nfs Developer lost+found vol pkg swapfile imagegeneration datadisk cdrom lib32 libx32 init __w _work docker-entrypoint.d entrypoint.sh sw firmlinks and the *.usr-is-merged names), in any letter case, with extra slashes, /./ or /../ before the name, a digit or underscore after it, a brace list (/{etc,usr}) or a one-character ? wildcard (/e?c); a first component that starts with a dot or contains a glob character; ~user; a chain of two or more ../; --option=/abs, an attached -C/, source=/, a redirect into /; the bare root (/, //, /., /.., /./, quoted, with an r/b/u/f prefix, or as an argument of a listed command such as ls, cd, find, grep, cat, cp, tar, git, test), cwd='/', open('/'), os.path.join('/', ...); os.sep and os.path.sep as a call argument, an assignment or inside abspath, realpath and normpath (not as a string-method argument such as .split(os.sep)); a home form (~/, $HOME, ${HOME, expanduser, Path.home, os.environ['HOME'], os.getenv('HOME'), os.environ.get('HOME'), pwd.getpwuid, pwd.getpwnam, cd ~, a bare cd, file: URIs, a chain of three ../); and, by syntax tree, os.symlink, os.link, symlink_to and hardlink_to with an absolute constant in any argument. It does not detect a path built at run time or by concatenation, a first component outside the list (unless it starts with a dot or contains a glob character), or anything in a file outside the name pattern. The shell checks (AC3) detect: ln or cp (also by /bin/ln or /usr/bin/ln) with the flags -s, -l, --symbolic, --symbolic-link in any position, or a hard ln, whose operand is absolute: starts with / (also / alone and //), ~, $'/..', a {/x,y} brace list, a ${V:-/x} ${V-/x} ${V=/x} ${V+/x} ${V:=/x} ${V:+/x} default (the ${V?/x} and ${V:?/x} forms are not detected), or an attached -t/x or --target-directory=/x, across a backslash-newline continuation; and a script in which a creator command word (mkdir, touch, cp, mv, ln, install, tee, mkfifo, mknod, dd of=, sed -i, git init or clone, after VAR=, sudo, env, command, exec, time, nice, xargs, !, then, do) or a redirect (>, >>, >| to a word that is not a descriptor &N, &-, a process substitution or /dev/null) appears outside comments, single and double quotes (except their $( ) and backtick substitutions), $(( )) and heredoc bodies, and mktemp is never a command word and python tempfile is never called outside a comment. Recorded residuals of the last verification passes (not fixed, by the advisor's hard stop): os.listdir('/dev/null') (or of /dev/urandom) reaches the operating system's NotADirectoryError, so "nothing else may be done to the devices" is not strictly enforced for listing a device (it does no harm: neither device is a directory); a spelling variant of the heredoc opener such as `echo \" "<<EOF"` (an escaped quote before a quoted opener) is not recognised as quoted, so a creator after it can be missed; and one comment in the shell lexer (the arithmetic blanking) was stale after the let change and has been corrected as a comment-only line. Go and Java tests are out of the static scan by decision; they run under the same guard only where discovery runs them in the Python interpreter.

## CHAIN

### REQ-CHAIN-006 — Check judges the candidates and signs what it found

The Check stage shall run, in one stage file beside Rebuild and off Build's output (the job check, and the job check-arm64 for the linux/arm64 artifact checks), every scanner the policy lists, the Gradle and Maven acceptance suites, the no-phone-home test, the FIPS start check and every customer-guide command against the exact candidate digests, as plain scripts that know nothing about signing, under Witness in three plainly named steps (scanners, acceptance, runtime) each limited to 9 minutes by the one shared helper, and sign its results as one Witness record per step under its own identity; it shall hold no registry or key access, and any failure shall stop the release and name Check.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-verify.yml; .github/workflows/release.yml; .github/workflows/acceptance.yml; bin/witnessed.sh; bin/check-stage.sh; bin/check-scan.sh; bin/check-fips.sh; bin/check-acceptance.sh; bin/check-guide.sh; bin/acceptance-gradle.sh; bin/acceptance-gradle-capped.sh; bin/acceptance-maven.sh; bin/acceptance-maven-capped.sh; bin/acceptance-egress.sh; bin/acceptance-k8s.sh; bin/acceptance-serve.sh; bin/install-kind.sh; .github/policy/scanners.json*

### REQ-CHAIN-007 — Release verifies everything first, then alone holds the credentials and publishes the exact bytes

The Release stage shall verify every earlier stage's signed record, in a fixed order and before any credential exists in its job, and only then use the apk signing key and the registry credentials, which no other job holds, to sign the released apks, publish by digest the exact bytes Build made and Rebuild and Check judged, read the registry back, sign everything a customer verifies keyless with a Rekor entry (images in both registries, SBOMs, lock files, the dependency evidence and the release policy), and attach the evidence to the release, without building anything and without creating a version tag.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-promote.yml; .github/workflows/release.yml; bin/release-verify.sh; bin/release-apks.sh; bin/release-publish.sh; bin/release-sign.sh; bin/release-assets.sh; .github/policy/chain-scripts.json*

> ADVISOR RULINGS (Oct 9, on the read-back). (a) A release candidate verifies exactly like a final release, so the tag rule is vX.Y.Z and vX.Y.Z-rc.N and nothing else; PR 1's policy make --tag must accept the same two shapes (its tests and code are on the PR 1 branch and need the same widening). (b) The release policy is signed with cosign, keyless, under Release's identity, so it has a Rekor entry a customer can check; Witness records stay extra evidence. (c) Signatures are made in both registries. (d) The dry-run proof of the whole chain (REQ-CHAIN-001-AC5) must be green before the cutover merge into main, not before each merge into chain-v030 (advisor confirmed). CUTOVER RULE (advisor 0341): PR 4 merges into the integration branch chain-v030 only; the live chain on main is untouched until the one cutover pull request, which has its own read-back, a final whole-diff review round and names the switch moment. A v* tag is the owner's; the first real run is the owner's rc tag. Release creates no tag. THE WITNESS WRAPPING is the one seam shared with PR 2 and 3 (owner's rule 68 amendment, Oct 9, and the readability request): every Witness step runs through the single helper bin/witnessed.sh STEP SCRIPT with timeout 540 inside it; the stage file never repeats Witness flags. Release has five such steps (release-verify, release-apks, release-publish, release-sign, release-assets) so that a credential reaches only the step that needs it and a step stays far below the ten-minute Fulcio certificate. PROPOSED/UNVERIFIED: the script names and command lines of bin/release-*.sh; the tool that re-signs an apk with the stored key (melange sign is assumed; cache-3f's apk-tool.py signer reports assembly.rsa.pub, release.rsa.pub or unsigned and is fixed by cache's tests); the copy tool (crane, pinned by checksum through bin/install-scanner.sh); the registry-state check before publishing; the artifact names images and apks; the floating tags (REQ-REL-009 moves them for finals only); and that cosign's bundle for a sign-blob holds a Rekor entry (tlogEntries) in the shape PR 1 verifies; that PR 1's stage-start accepts --rekor-stub for Sign's provenance (else one more verify line); the crane entry of bin/install-scanner.sh (version, asset names, CRANE_BASE_URL; tested by bin/chain-install-crane-test.sh). The environment named release restricted to v* tags is the owner's setting (note only, no test). This PR cannot be run end to end before PRs 1 to 3 exist.
